done.why: After I died and was sent back, the well bucket stayed at the top. I couldn't get back up to the Tea Room, and waiting and pulling the rope did nothing. Most other exits were blocked by rockfalls marked 'will have to wait'.

about: A first slice of an underground cavern adventure in the style of Zork II. It has a barrow, a cavern with a ravine, a formal garden, a carousel room, a riddle door, a magic well, a mad tea room and a machine room. A wizard casts random spells on you as you move.

moments.note: Filling the teapot at the ford and riding the bucket up the well felt like a clever chain of steps.
The robot pushed the triangular button, which stopped the carousel.
Taking the sphere dropped a cage on me. The poison gas killed me in a couple of turns, with no way out and no warning.
Death sent me back to the barrow with an empty inventory. I had to collect my things again.
I couldn't get the bucket down from the top of the well, so the Tea Room was out of reach.
Garden exits led to odd places. North from the garden took me to the Dark Tunnel, and the unicorn seemed to be an illusion.

wished: Reach the rest of the map past the rockfalls.
Get the bucket back down to the bottom of the well.
Try the cakes and the hole in the Tea Room.
Know how to survive the sphere cage.

lines.line: As you reach for the sphere, a solid steel cage falls from the ceiling to entrap you.
lines.why: This was the trap that killed me.

lines.line: There is now a puddle in the bottom of the wooden bucket. The bucket rises and comes to a stop.
lines.why: This was the best puzzle payoff.

fun.why: I enjoyed the puzzles, but the death and the stuck well hurt.

engagement.why: I had clear goals until the well blocked me.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair, but the cage death was abrupt and the dead end was not clear.

interestingness.why: It reworks familiar Zork II material with some new twists, such as the wizard's spells and the etchings.

prose.why: The prose is crisp and echoes the original, and the blocked-passage lines have charm.
